item.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.14847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$
item.dc:creator: Sotiria Chatzimarkou

item.title: Entropy-degree rigidity for non-collapsed $RCD$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the entropy-degree theorem for continuous maps from a closed orientable non-collapsed $RCD(K,N)$ space $X$ to a closed negatively curved locally symmetric $N$-manifold $Y$, with $N \geq 3$. In the equality case, under a fundamental group index condition, we show the space is isometric to a smooth locally symmetric Riemannian manifold, and the map is homotopic to a Riemannian covering.
item.dc:creator: P. Su\'arez-Serrato

item.title: A Chord-Arc Estimate for Graphical Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.15157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an interior chord-arc estimate for graphical hypersurfaces without an a priori gradient bound, which is not restricted to balls on the scale of their curvature. As a main application we derive an in-radius lower bound depending on the curvature which then also implies Heinz-type estimates for minimal graphs and uniform area bounds for graphical hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Reznikov

item.title: Liouville type results for super-$p$-biharmonic immersions and $p$-biharmonic submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.15212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a weak notion of $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion into Euclidean space, formulated through a divergence inequality for the mean curvature vector. This class naturally extends the $\varepsilon$-superbiharmonic immersions previously introduced by the third author while remaining well-defined for all $p>1$, including the singular range $1<p<2$. We prove a Liouville-type rigidity theorem showing that every proper $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion is minimal provided \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac1{r^{2}} \int_{f^{-1}(B_r)} |\vec{H}| ^{q}\,d\mu=0 \] for some $q>p-\varepsilon$. This extends the corresponding superbiharmonic rigidity theorem to the $p$-biharmonic setting under a natural growth hypothesis. We also establish a minimality theorem for complete $p$-biharmonic immersions into Riemannian manifolds of non-positive sectional curvature under a polynomial growth assumption on the mean curvature. More precisely, if \[ \int_{B_r(x_0)} | \vec{H} | ^{\,q}\,d\mu = O(r^d) \] for some $q\ge0$ and $d>0$, then the immersion is minimal. For $q=0$ this recovers the polynomial volume-growth theorem of Cao--Luo \cite{CL16}, while for $q>0$ it provides a polynomial-growth analogue of Han's $L^q$-integrability rigidity theorem \cite{H15}.
item.dc:creator: Tien Dat Dinh, Nguyen Thac Dung, Glen Wheeler

item.title: Prescribed inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature flow on finite trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.15213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the image of the inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature map on finite edge-weighted trees. We prove that the prescribed curvature flow converges if and only if the target curvature is attainable, and that the convergence is exponential whenever it occurs. The key ingredient in the proof is a formulation of the prescribed curvature flow as the gradient flow of a convex functional.
item.dc:creator: Shuliang Bai, Haoxuan Cheng, Bobo Hua

item.title: Polynomial approximations to Calabi--Yau metrics on quartic K3 surfaces and quintic threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.15319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On the Fermat quartic K3 surface and the Fermat quintic threefold, we construct K\"ahler metrics from explicit rational polynomial potentials and bound their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics in integral tensor norms. For specified compact families of smooth quartic and quintic hypersurfaces near the Fermat hypersurfaces, we give a terminating algorithm that constructs polynomial K\"ahler metrics with prescribed pointwise bounds on their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics and on their Ricci forms. The resulting metrics converge to the Ricci-flat metrics in every $C^r$ norm, uniformly in the parameter.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Liangdi Zhang

item.title: Classification of G-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces G/H with G simple
item.description: arXiv:2611.15336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the $G$-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces $G/H$, where $G$ is a compact connected simple Lie group and $H$ is an arbitrary closed subgroup. We give the complete list of nonnormal metrics, including their parameter conditions and the possible mixing between equivalent isotropy summands. The proof uses rigidity criteria for arbitrary cometric operators, reductions through centralizers, and the stabilizers of the relevant representations. For every fixed pair $(G,H)$, the space spanned by the $G$-g.o. cometrics has dimension at most three, and we determine the equality cases. We also compare the classification with the compact weakly symmetric pairs and explain why the choice of the transitive group is essential.
item.dc:creator: Huibin Chen, Zhiqi Chen, Zaili Yan, Fuhai Zhu

item.title: Harmonic functions and the topology of 3-manifolds under nonnegative scalar curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.15384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish and recover some results about noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and some topological assumptions. Firstly, we apply the work in Oronzio \cite{Oro1,Oro2} to obtain a nonexistence result of the harmonic function. Secondly, we use the argument in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} to establish a rigidity result, which states that such manifold is isometric to the warped product of a flat tours and a half line. Finally, we recover a topological result in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} via a different argument.
item.dc:creator: Jiannan Chen, Haiping Fu

item.title: Hyperbolicity Notions on Complete Non-Compact Complex Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.15396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gromov's K\"ahler hyperbolicity, extended by McMullen to complete manifolds of finite volume and bounded geometry, has non-K\"ahler analogues (balanced, SKT, Gauduchon and divisorial hyperbolicity) that have so far been studied only on compact manifolds. We define these notions for complete Hermitian manifolds and prove the following. A manifold carrying a balanced metric and a Hermitian metric with bounded $(\partial+\bar\partial)$-potentials satisfies a Cheeger inequality, so its fundamental group is non-amenable in the compact case. K\"ahler and SKT hyperbolic manifolds are Brody hyperbolic, and balanced and Gauduchon hyperbolic manifolds are divisorially hyperbolic, without any compactness assumption. Products give complete non-compact non-K\"ahler examples. A non-compact surface may be divisorially hyperbolic without being Brody hyperbolic. Finally, no functorial pseudo-distance characterises divisorial hyperbolicity.}
item.dc:creator: Samir Marouani

item.title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.15400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.
item.dc:creator: Zixuan Qiu, Pengshuai Shi, Ruijun Wu

item.title: A note on equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion
item.description: arXiv:2611.15562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we introduce an equivariant version of twisted holomorphic analytic torsion for the twisted Dolbeault complex on a complex manifold equipped with an action of a compact Lie group. Our construction is motivated by Ray and Singer's holomorphic analytic torsion, by the equivariant analytic torsion developed for elliptic complexes with group actions, notably in the work of Donnelly and later in the holomorphic setting by Bismut, and by Mathai and Wu's twisted analytic torsion for the twisted de Rham complex. Using pseudodifferential operators and the equivariant noncommutative residue, we define the equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion. We also state its variation formulas under changes of the metric and of the twisting element, and present its functorial properties.
item.dc:creator: Minxiang Yuan

item.title: Weighted minimal surfaces in H2 x R invariant under hyperbolic translations
item.description: arXiv:2611.15570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR, namely, surfaces that arise as critical points of a weighted area functional, where the corresponding weight depends only on the height function associated with the second factor R. We refer to these surfaces as {\phi}-minimal surfaces. For a class of increasing and concave weight potential functions {\phi}, we focus our attention on height-weighted minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of H2xR that act trivially on R and act by hyperbolic translations in H2. Through a detailed analysis of the corresponding three-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations, we present families of entire graphs, graphs over half-spaces of H2 that are asymptotic to vertical planes, winglike surfaces, and surfaces whose height function has no minimum. These families show that the hyperbolic-invariant setting is considerably richer than the rotational and parabolic settings. For the class of potential functions {\phi} we consider, they also allow us to classify all weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR that are invariant under hyperbolic translations.
item.dc:creator: Katianny Rosa Freitas, Ant\'onio Mart\'inez, Jo\~ao Paulo dos Santos

item.title: Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.15637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.
item.dc:creator: Daheng Min

item.title: HKT-Einstein metrics on circle bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.15697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a construction of hyper-Hermitian structures on total spaces of circle bundles over 3-quasi-Sasakian manifolds. We study the HKT-Einstein equation in this setting, proving that a large family of non-homogeneous hyper-complex manifolds admit compatible HKT-Einstein metrics with positive Einstein factor. We also show that the hyper-Hermitian structures on such circle bundles are quaternionic balanced or quaternionic Gauduchon if and only if they are HKT. Finally, the HKT-Einstein condition is investigated under the twist construction.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Marcocci

item.title: Entropic Ricci bounds at conic singularities and boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2611.15796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study synthetic Ricci bounds and related rigidity phenomena in conic and boundary neighborhoods through the behavior of entropy along optimal transports. For cones over manifolds, we show that two-sided entropic Ricci bounds at the vertex force the fiber to have constant sectional curvature 1, while non-trivial quotient singularities, such as Euclidean cones over spherical space forms, remain admissible. An analogous rigidity holds for Riemannian manifolds with conic singularities. We also give a local characterization of boundary convexity in terms of entropic lower Ricci bounds, based on a direct optimal transport argument.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhao Li

item.title: Poisson and Jacobi structures on quadratic Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.15800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Poisson and Jacobi structures compatible with quadratic structures on finite-dimensional Lie algebras, mostly over fields of characteristic zero. Building on the theory of generalized double extensions, we give necessary and sufficient reconstruction criteria for the skew operators preserving a marked isotropic ideal, allowing degenerate operators, a nonabelian quadratic quotient, and the full generalized extension data. Recalling the characterization of quadratic Poisson structures in terms of skew-symmetric solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation, we combine the ambient bracket reconstruction of Kostant and Meyer with prescribed symplectic leaf data to reconstruct Poisson structures whose characteristic subalgebra is nondegenerate for the quadratic form. We express the standard algebraic Jacobi equations through the invariant form and obtain analogous reconstruction results for nondegenerate characteristic subalgebras. Particular attention is given to the contact and locally conformally symplectic cases. A common cochain framework identifies the remaining scalar obstruction in third cohomology in the Poisson case and in the Jacobi branch whose Euler element belongs to the marked ideal, with coefficients in a one dimensional module in the latter case. Our reconstruction results yield systematic procedures for constructing quadratic Poisson structures in dimension $n+2k$ from those in dimension $n$, and recover the earlier quadratic symplectic extension formulas when the Poisson operator is invertible. Explicit examples illustrate the applicability of the theory, including oscillator algebras, the five-dimensional Lie algebra $A_{5,3}$, and Poisson structures associated with the curvature tensor of a bi-invariant metric.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Arsie, Fabricio Valencia

item.title: Generic equivariant simplicity of the spectrum of Laplace-type operators with finite symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.15832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for generic elements in three natural families of Laplace-type differential operators on smooth manifolds, which are equivariant with respect to a finite symmetry group, all the eigenspaces are irreducible representations. In other words, the spectrum of these operators is generically equivariantly simple. The three families of operators with symmetry are Schr\"odinger operators parametrized by the potential, going back to the work of Wigner, Laplace-Beltrami operators parametrized by invariant Riemannian metrics and conformal Laplacians parametrized by invariant metrics in a given conformal class. The latter two results extend prior work of Zelditch for certain free group actions and resolve, for finite group actions, a well-known open question raised by Guillemin and Yau. Our approach stems from methods developed by Wendl and Doan-Walpuski to address equivariant transversality in symplectic topology.
item.dc:creator: Egor Morozov, Egor Shelukhin

item.title: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.15912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Albachiara Cogo

item.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
item.description: arXiv:2611.16101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,\alpha): x\in U, \alpha \in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),\alpha(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).
item.dc:creator: Hugo Murilo Rodrigues, Ryuichi Fukuoka

item.title: Holomorphic Sectional Curvature of Flag Manifolds via K\"ahler Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.16181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an alternative proof of Li and Petersen's theorem that every invariant K\"ahler metric on a compact generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For a unitary partial flag manifold, we realize the given metric by K\"ahler reduction of a Hermitian vector space. The defining equations place the level set on a sphere of radius \varrho, where the radial component of its second fundamental form gives the explicit lower bound 4/\varrho2 through the quotient curvature formula. Finally, we use a holomorphic isometric totally geodesic embedding to transfer the bound to generalized flag manifolds of every Lie type.
item.dc:creator: Ching-Hsien Lee

item.title: Rigidity of compact quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary and low-dimensional focal sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.16314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we investigate nontrivial compact m-quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary, m > 1 and constant scalar curvature. We first prove that such a manifold is rigid whenever the set of critical points of its potential function is totally geodesic, which extends to quasi-Einstein manifolds a theorem of Li, Li, Ou, Qu, Wu and Zhou for shrinking Ricci solitons. Then, we prove that, in every dimension, this set is totally geodesic whenever it has dimension two or three, so that the manifold is rigid in this case. The proof is based on a Bochner identity for the covariant derivative of the Ricci tensor at the points of this set. In particular, every such manifold of dimension five is rigid. Finally, we obtain rigidity in arbitrary dimension under an integral Weyl pinching condition when the set of critical points has dimension four.
item.dc:creator: Matheus Andrade Ribeiro de Moura Hor\'acio

item.title: Invariant complex Finsler metrics on reductive complex homogeneous spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.16370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M=G/H,J)$ be a reductive complex homogeneous space and $F$ be a $G$-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on $M$. Using the adapted $(1,0)$-frame field obtained by parallel transformation with respect to the canonical connection on $M$, we obtain the necessary and sufficient condition for $F$ to be a K\"ahler-Finsler metric (resp. weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metric) in terms of Lie-bracket. The curvature tensor of the complex Rund connection associated to $F$ is then decomposed into an algebraic part and a derivative part, yielding explicit formulas for the holomorphic bisectional curvature and holomorphic sectional curvature of $F$, respectively. As an application, we give a Lie-theoretic proof of the rigidity theorem: every $G$-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on a complex symmetric manifold $M=G/H$ is necessarily a K\"ahler--Berwald metric.
item.dc:creator: Kuankuan Luo, Chunping Zhong

item.title: Hessian sectional curvatures of conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.16381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds generalize Hessian manifolds. Shima introduced Hessian sectional curvature in 1995 as an invariant for studying Hessian structures. We extend this invariant to conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds and study related curvature conditions and invariants. Our main results are as follows. For connected Hessian manifolds of dimension at least two, we characterize constant Hessian sectional curvature (CHC) by pointwise orthogonal invariance. We call conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds satisfying this invariance condition weakly CHC. We classify connected weakly CHC statistical manifolds of dimension at least two whose cubic forms are parallel with respect to the Levi-Civita connection. This classification characterizes the non-Hessian statistical structures induced on the classical hyperbolic affine spheres $xyz=c>0$ in the positive octant. We also introduce principal Hessian curvatures and show that they form a complete invariant for left-invariant Hessian structures on $\mathbb{R}^n$ up to statistical isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Hikozo Kobayashi

item.title: Kobayashi distance to submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold
item.description: arXiv:2611.16571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that totally geodesic hypersurfaces are at infinite Kobayashi distance in a Kobayashi hyperbolic Riemannian manifold. To do this, we prove a Schwarz lemma on minimal maps with a uniform control on their Laplacians. Finally we give a full characterisation of submanifolds at infinite distance on spaces of constant sectional curvature in dimension at least 4.
item.dc:creator: Keeran Poirot

item.title: On compact homogeneous Locally conformal symplectic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.16625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A locally conformally symplectic (LCS) structure on a manifold $M$ is a pair $(\eta,\omega)$ consisting of a closed $1$-form $\eta$ called Lee form and a nondegenerate $2$-form $\omega$ satisfying \[ d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega. \] We classify compact connected homogeneous LCS manifolds with nonzero Lee form. To this end, we construct three explicit families of pairs $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected simply connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup such that $G/K$ is compact, the $G$-action is almost effective, and $G/K$ admits a $G$-invariant LCS structure. We show that every compact connected homogeneous LCS manifold with nonzero Lee form arises from one of these families. Moreover, each such manifold is LCS-isomorphic to a product $(S/H_d)\times S^1$, where $S$ is a compact connected simply connected semisimple Lie group and $S/H_d$ carries an $S$-invariant contact form $\alpha$. Under this identification, the LCS structure is given by \[ \eta=\pi_2^*\xi,\qquad \omega=d(\pi_1^*\alpha)+\pi_1^*\alpha\wedge\eta, \] where $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ are the projections onto the two factors and $\xi$ is a nowhere-vanishing $1$-form on $S^1$. This description also yields topological consequences for compact homogeneous LCS manifolds. In particular, none of these compact homogeneous LCS manifolds admits a symplectic structure, even without any invariance assumption. As a consequence, we show that in dimension four the underlying manifolds are precisely $L(d,1)\times S^1$, where $L(d,1)$ is a three-dimensional lens space. In dimension eight, we obtain families arising from seven-dimensional lens spaces and Aloff--Wallach spaces, including infinitely many distinct topological types.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Boucetta

item.title: Complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional: examples and rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.16712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional \[ g\mapsto\int_M S_g^2\,\dv_g, \] with criticality understood under compactly supported variations, focusing on rigidity phenomena and nontrivial examples. In dimension three, we prove that every complete critical metric is scalar-flat, without any additional assumption. In dimension four, we construct complete non-Einstein critical metrics with bounded, nonconstant negative scalar curvature. In every dimension $n\geq5$, we show that either $S_g\equiv 0$ or $S_g<0$ everywhere, and a new argument proves scalar-flatness whenever $S_g \in L^p$ for some $0<p\leq P_n$, where $P_n>2$ is an explicit threshold. Moreover, we construct complete critical metrics with bounded, negative scalar curvature, decaying to zero at infinity. These examples establish the optimality of our rigidity threshold $P_n$ in dimension six and in every dimension $n\geq10$. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first complete critical metrics for this functional that are neither scalar-flat nor Einstein.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Catino, Paolo Mastrolia, Dario Daniele Monticelli

item.title: Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.16810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $\pi$. We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints. We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.
item.dc:creator: Yen-Chang Huang (Department of Applied Mathematics, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan), Yan-Hong Chen (Department of Applied Mathematics, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan)

item.title: Morse index, nullity and Jacobi fields of homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.16813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Morse index and normal nullity of all linearly full homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics. These invariants satisfy a common relation involving only the ambient dimension and the induced Gauss curvature. We also prove that every normal Jacobi field is integrable through minimal immersions.
item.dc:creator: Qing Chen, Shuping Huang, Shoulan Yi

item.title: A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
item.description: arXiv:2611.16908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a rigorous, constructive proof that there exists a Ricci-flat K\"ahler metric on the Fermat quartic hypersurface, independently of Yau's famous theorem, along with an explicit and accurate analytic approximation to the metric. The proof combines numerical techniques to obtain the approximately Ricci flat metric, a fixed point theorem to prove existence, and verified numerics to get the bounds used by the fixed point theorem. The method is general and we discuss the computational issues in applying it to other manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Michael R. Douglas, Javier G\'omez-Serrano, Fabian Lehmann, Daniel Platt, Yidi Qi

item.title: Weak stability of Ricci flow with almost WPIC1 curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.16910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove weak $L^\infty$ stability for complete, non-collapsed Ricci flows with almost WPIC1 curvature and scaling-invariant curvature bounds. Small $L^\infty$ perturbations of the initial metric admit Ricci-DeTurck flows which remain uniformly close to the background flow and depend Lipschitz continuously on the initial data. This extends an earlier stability theorem of the first and third authors with Lai.
item.dc:creator: Pak-Yeung Chan, Lucas Lavoyer, Man-Chun Lee

item.title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
item.description: arXiv:2611.16911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Takeuchi

item.title: On real-analytic non-degeneracy of left-symmetric algebras in dimension 3
item.description: arXiv:2611.16954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that any three-dimensional differentially non-degenerate left-symmetric algebra over $\mathbb R$ is non-degenerate both in the formal and real-analytic categories via the correspondence with Nijenhuis operators.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Manenti, Serena Scapucci

item.title: Non-existence of closed embedded magnetic geodesics
item.description: arXiv:2611.16960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a counterexample to S. Novikov's 1982 conjecture that every Riemannian $2$-sphere contains a closed embedded curve of curvature $c$ for every $c>0$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Ketover

item.title: Non self-similar solutions to the Ricci flow coming out of metric cones
item.description: arXiv:2611.16976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an asymptotically conical unstable expanding gradient Ricci soliton, we provide the existence of a family of Ricci flows starting at the same metric cone up to isometry. Moreover, the family of solutions we construct is shown to be parametrized by positive modes of the weighted Lichnerowicz operator associated to the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton. Each solution of this family is shown not to be induced by an expanding gradient Ricci soliton. If the background expander has no non-trivial infinitesimal deformations, we show furthermore that the solutions we provide are not self-similar. We finally prove that solutions are distinct up to isometries preserving the potential function of the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton.
item.dc:creator: Alix Deruelle, Tristan Ozuch, Felix Schulze

item.title: Hinge comparison and excess estimates via modified Hessian bounds on manifolds with density
item.description: arXiv:2611.17039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study geometric consequences of modified Hessian estimates on Riemannian manifolds with density. For general radial functions, we derive tensorial, spectral, and trace identities for the modified Hessian in the original metric. We also establish a comparison identity relating the modified Hessians of two radial functions and characterize when they are proportional. We then prove a hinge comparison theorem under an upper bound on the modified Hessian, yielding a weighted law of cosines and lower bounds for the excess function. Finally, under nonnegative weighted sectional curvature and suitable density control assumptions, we obtain an Abresch-Gromoll-type upper excess estimate.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Ng

item.title: Spinorial geometry of Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.17195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a pair of spinorial equations, generalizing the internal Killing spinor equations of Type I supergravity, and show that they characterize several classes of Bismut-Hermitian-Einstein structures on six-dimensional Riemannian spin manifolds. We show that in this framework the local reduction to a four-dimensional transverse Hermitian geometry is provided by two canonical, commuting, Bismut-parallel Killing vector fields arising as bilinears in the Killing spinors, without assuming compactness. In one class, the transverse geometry is conformally Kahler and both compact and non-compact solutions exist. We also discuss variants that do not admit compact solutions, one of which has hyper-Hermitian transverse geometry. We discuss the relation of these structures to the Hull-Strominger system with closed three-form and to five-dimensional Gauntlett-Kim geometries and provide explicit embeddings in Type I, Type IIB and massive Type IIA supergravity, as well as in generalized supergravity. We illustrate our results with a number of examples, both compact and non-compact.
item.dc:creator: Beatrice Brienza, Matteo Kevin Crisafio, Anna Fino, Dario Martelli

item.title: Stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions seven and eight
item.description: arXiv:2611.17249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish optimal sheet separation estimates for stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions up to seven, using an iteration argument in the nonlocal approximation theory of Chan-Dipierro-Serra-Valdinoci. These estimates imply that every stable $s$-minimal hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a hyperplane when $s$ is close to $1$. More generally, every finite Morse index $s$-minimal set in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a half-space. We also establish a compactness theorem for stable $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$. We prove uniform curvature and area estimates for their links and show that, as $s \uparrow 1$, they subconverge graphically in $C^{2,\alpha}$, either with multiplicity one to a classical stable minimal cone, or with multiplicity two to a hyperplane. The stability of Lawson and axisymmetric $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$ shows that these results are optimal.
item.dc:creator: Serena Dipierro, Joaquim Serra, Raphael Tsiamis, Enrico Valdinoci

item.title: Stability for the Bray-Brendle-Neves Scalar Sphere Rigidity Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.17263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^3,g)$ be a closed and oriented 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\pi_2(M)\neq 0$ and let $A_{\pi_2}(M,g)$ denote the least area among homotopically nontrivial two-spheres in $M$. By a theorem of Bray-Brendle-Neves, $A_{\pi_2}(M,g)\inf_M R_g \leq 8\pi$ with equality characterizing the cylindrical geometry $S^2\times\mathbb{R}$. Motivated by Sormani's questions on volume preserving intrinsic flat stability for scalar curvature rigidity problems, we study the almost equality regime of this theorem. We build, using Sweeney's tunnel construction, a sequence satisfying $A_{\pi_2}(M_j,g_j)\inf_{M_j} R_{g_j} \rightarrow 8\pi$ with uniformly bounded volume and diameter whose volume preserving intrinsic flat limit is not the Bray-Brendle-Neves rigidity space, showing that stability fails in general. We then prove stability in two special cases: for sequences of rotationally symmetric metrics (with non-collapsing assumptions) and for sequences of manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature.
item.dc:creator: Carolina Ruviaro

item.title: Nonrigidity of smooth tight surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.17269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct smooth isometric embeddings of closed surfaces of positive genus in Euclidean 3-space which are tight, i.e., have minimal total positive curvature, but are not congruent. These embeddings agree outside a compact subset of the region of negative curvature, and enclose different volumes. Thus the rigidity theorem of Alexandrov for analytic tight surfaces does not hold in the smooth category, which settles problems of Nirenberg and Banchoff-Kuhnel.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Ghomi, Hongda Qiu, Matteo Raffaelli, Yuetong Zhang

item.title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.17319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.
item.dc:creator: C. S. Shahbazi

item.title: A transition calculus for 0-pseudodifferential operators with applications to gas giant geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.04191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A gas giant Riemannian metric $g$ on a compact $n$-dimensional manifold-with-boundary $M$ blows up at the boundary $\partial M$ at the rate $1/x^\alpha$, for $\alpha \in (0,2)$, where $x \in C^\infty(M)$ is a boundary-defining function. Such metrics arise in the modeling of acoustic waves in gaseous planets. De Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykk\"{a}nen-Mazzeo [arXiv:2403.05475] showed that, if $\alpha > 2/n$, the Laplace-Beltrami operator $\Delta_g$ is essentially self-adjoint and has discrete spectrum. Moreover, its spectrum is stable under truncations of $M$. The proof leverages the 0-calculus of Mazzeo-Melrose. We extend this theory by introducing a 0-transition calculus for studying families of 0-operators. We demonstrate a parametrix construction for $\Delta_g$ that is stable under truncations. Using this, we study the behavior of the resolvent of $\Delta_g$ under truncation and extend the characterization of the spectrum obtained by de Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykk\"{a}nen-Mazzeo. In particular, we prove that (on appropriate functional-analytic domains) simple eigenvalues admit asymptotic expansions in the truncation parameter $\epsilon$ and that the corresponding eigenfunctions admit joint asymptotic expansions in $(\epsilon, x)$.
item.dc:creator: Andy Yin

item.title: Euclidean filling inequalities in CAT(0) spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.13159v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We clarify and streamline OpenAI's proof of the sharp Euclidean filling inequalities in CAT(0) spaces. We extend the result to complete spaces without assuming properness or compact support, and we establish rigidity in the equality case.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Lytchak

item.title: The Isoperimetric Flow and Synthetic Scalar Curvature for Causal Variational Principles
item.description: arXiv:2611.14265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An isoperimetric flow is introduced in the setting of causal variational principles. Describing the whole space by the support of a minimizing measure, we define an area functional on subsets by a surface layer integral. Mean curvature is defined via the first variation of this area functional. Using the method of minimizing movement, the isoperimetric flow is constructed as a Lipschitz curve of measures with prescribed volume change. As illustrating examples, we introduce and analyze ``smeared variants'' of the mean curvature flow in Euclidean space and on a Riemannian manifold. In these examples, it is shown that our area functional coincides with the usual area up to specified curvature corrections. As an application of our general results, by analyzing the volume and area of small isoperimetric balls, we introduce notions of local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature.
item.dc:creator: Felix Finster, Franz Gmeineder, Margarita Kraus

item.title: Making Poisson {\sigma} again - an \'etude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
item.description: arXiv:2611.14784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Poisson $\sigma$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $\Sigma$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = \Sigma \times G \to \Sigma$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,\omega)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,\Pi)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = \Sigma \times M \to \Sigma$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $\Sigma$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,\Pi)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $\omega$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.
item.dc:creator: Rafa{\l} R. Suszek

item.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.16068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.
item.dc:creator: Milena Brockhof, Giovane Galindo, Ludmil Katzarkov, Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins

item.title: Generalized Kosmann derivative and symmetry operators on Dirac structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.16309v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a spinorial symmetry framework for metric Dirac structures in $H$-twisted exact Courant algebroids. A generalized metric equips a Dirac structure with an intrinsic Riemannian Lie-algebroid geometry and identifies it isometrically with the positive subbundle of the generalized tangent bundle. For sections preserving the generalized metric, we prove an exact intertwining between the positive-spinor Kosmann--Dorfman action and the intrinsic Kosmann derivative. The comparison is independent of the auxiliary compatible generalized connection. Within the intrinsic geometry we derive Killing--Yano (KY) and conformal Killing--Yano (CKY) integrability identities, construct Killing-spinor-preserving operators from odd special KY and even special closed CKY forms, and obtain these forms from Hermitian bilinears of Killing spinors with imaginary Killing number. We illustrate the framework on a global Dirac structure over $S^2\times S^1$ with nontrivial $H$-flux class and rank-two anchor. Its spin connection and symmetry operators are explicit, and its Killing-spinor space is a transverse family $C^\infty(S^1,\mathbb C^2)$. Finally, intrinsic Killing sections act on Killing spinors by a Lie algebra representation. For a graph Dirac structure over $S^3$, the odd Jacobi identity of the Hermitian-current bracket fails by a phase, and adjoining a single even phase generator yields a Lie superalgebra. These results connect generalized isometries, hidden spinorial symmetries, and flux-sensitive Lie-algebroid geometry.
item.dc:creator: \"{U}mit Ertem, \"{O}zg\"{u}r A\c{c}{\i}k, \"{O}zg\"{u}r Kelek\c{c}i

item.title: The Bolza Surface Does Not Locally Minimize the Diameter Function
item.description: arXiv:2611.16340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the diameter function on the Teichm\"uller space of closed hyperbolic Riemann surfaces. Although the Bolza surface maximizes the systole among hyperbolic surfaces of genus 2, its extremal behavior with respect to the diameter function is less clear. Using first variations of distances at diameter pairs and linear programming duality, we establish a sufficient criterion for a surface not to be a local minimizer of the diameter function. More precisely, we show that if each diameter pair can be assigned a simple closed geodesic formed by two minimizing geodesic segments joining its endpoints, with distinct assigned geodesics pairwise disjoint, then a deformation varying only the length parameters in Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates strictly decreases the diameter. The assigned geodesics extend to a pants decomposition, and the decrease is detected by a strictly negative upper bound for the first-order variation of the diameter. We then apply this criterion to the Bolza surface and prove that it is not a local minimizer of the diameter function on the Teichm\"uller space of genus 2.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Matsuda, Keita Yamazaki

item.title: Renormalized volume, Generalized Loewner energy, and Grunsky determinant of multiply connected domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.16503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define and study three M\"obius invariant functionals for multiply connected planar domains with finitely many boundary components: the Loewner energy, the renormalized volume, and the Grunsky determinant. Using quasiconformal variations, we prove that when the boundary curves are sufficiently regular, the three functionals differ only by a modulus-dependent constant. We also prove that the Loewner energy is finite if and only if every boundary curve is a Weil--Petersson quasicircle. Moreover, we prove that the three functionals all attain their unique extremal value at the circle domains. In particular, the Loewner energy is zero if and only if it is evaluated at a circle domain. Finally, we use the minimization of Loewner energy to give a new proof of the finitely connected version of Koebe uniformization theorem.
item.dc:creator: Yan Luo

item.title: Chern characteristic classes of normal bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds in generalized flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.16837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$. The combination of representation theory and algebraic geometry allows to derive analogous properties for the isotropic Grassmannians $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$ via their embeddings in $\mathrm{Gr}(m, k)$. Then the induced CW structure yields the additive structure on the cohomology of $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$, and consequently leads to the calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Knesel, Petr Somberg

item.title: The uniqueness of smooth stationary black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.16853v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal Kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. The method is to apply Harrison transform to construct a family of solutions of Einstein--Maxwell equations. Combining null area comparison with the area-charge inequality, we show that, in the limiting transformed geometry, the bifurcate sphere has area radius one and constant electric and magnetic flux densities, with the original ADM mass normalized to $M=1$. These identities imply the technical assumptions of Ionescu--Klainerman, yielding the identification with Kerr.
item.dc:creator: Yishen Huang, Jiongyue Li, Junbin Li, Xi-Ping Zhu

item.title: Eigenvalue estimates of the drifted Cheng-Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2107.09135v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish universal eigenvalue inequalities for a drifted Cheng--Yau operator on bounded domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Our approach combines a universal quadratic eigenvalue inequality for operators in divergence form with a Rauch-type comparison theorem and a Bochner-type formula. We evaluate the geometric terms in this quadratic inequality under suitable assumptions on the radial behavior of the coefficient tensor and the drifting function, together with curvature pinching conditions. In the general setting, we establish a Rauch-type comparison theorem for the Cheng--Yau operator and derive two auxiliary estimates from its Bochner-type formula. We then prove integral estimates of independent interest and apply them to obtain the desired eigenvalue inequalities for both the Cheng--Yau operator and the drifted Laplacian, recovering known inequalities for the Laplacian. We also establish a rigidity result for the Cheng--Yau operator on a class of bounded annular domains in pinched Cartan--Hadamard manifolds. In Euclidean space, this result can be applied, for instance, with the potential function of the Gaussian shrinking soliton. The hyperbolic space is treated separately in two settings, one exploiting the conformal relation between its metric and the Euclidean metric, and the other via its warped product structure, reducing the problem to one dimension. We extend the hyperbolic construction of the fundamental gap for the Laplacian to a class of operators in divergence form. Examples are provided to illustrate the scope and applicability of our results.
item.dc:creator: J\'ulio C. M. da Fonseca, Jos\'e N. V. Gomes

item.title: Variation of Hodge structures for non-K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2205.09274v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we discuss unpolarized, complex variation of Hodge structures for non-K\"ahler manifolds. In particular, consider a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds with central fiber $X$. Suppose that the inclusion of complexes $(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\hookrightarrow (A^\bullet(X),d)$ induces injective maps \[ H^j(F^pA^\bullet(X),d)\longrightarrow H^j(A^\bullet(X),d),\qquad j=k,\ k+1. \] Under this condition, we show that the period map is holomorphic and transversal. An essential ingredient for the proof is a deformation theory of filtered $(p,q)$-forms. We prove a jumping formula for filtered de Rham cohomology and obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for its dimension to be invariant under deformation of complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Wei Xia

item.title: Leafwise positive scalar curvature and the Rosenberg index
item.description: arXiv:2502.02325v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be a closed spin manifold, in this paper, we show that if there is a foliation $(M,F)$ and a Riemannian metric on $M$ that has leafwise positive scalar curvature then the Rosenberg index of $M$ is zero.
item.dc:creator: Guangxiang Su, Zelin Yi

item.title: Classification of Certain Rational Isoparametric Functions on Damek-Ricci Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2505.10608v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify isoparametric functions on Damek-Ricci spaces which can be written in terms of the standard coordinates $(v,z,t)$ on the half-space model as a polynomial function divided by $t$. Regular level sets of the functions in our classification encompass almost all previously known examples of isoparametric hypersufaces in Damek-Ricci space and also yield new ones. For the new examples, the focal varieties are determined and the mean curvatures of the regular level sets are expressed as a function of the distance from the focal variety. We also study the exceptional case of tubes about $\mathbb R\mathbf H^k$ in $\mathbb C\mathbf H^k$, which are isoparametric, but cannot be obtained as the level sets of any function in our classification. We show that these tubes are level sets of a polynomial function divided by $t^2$, and that analogous functions on Damek-Ricci spaces can be isoparametric only in the case of $\mathbb C\mathbf H^k$.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs Csik\'os, M\'arton Horv\'ath

item.title: The mean curvature flow of subgroups on Lie groups of dimension three
item.description: arXiv:2505.17892v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we study the existence of solutions to the Mean Curvature Flow for which the initial condition has the structure of a two-dimensional Lie subgroup within a Lie group of dimension three. We consider Lie groups with a fixed left-invariant metric and first observe that if the Lie group is unimodular, then every Lie subgroup is a minimal surface (hence a trivial solution). For this reason we focus on non-unimodular Lie groups, finding the evolution of every Lie subgroup of dimension 2 (within a 3 dimensional Lie group). These evolutions are self-similar for abelian subgroups (i.e. evolve by isometries), but not self-similar in the other cases.
item.dc:creator: Romina M. Arroyo, Gabriela P. Ovando, Mariel S\'aez

item.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
item.description: arXiv:2509.08588v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $\lambda_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $\lambda_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.
item.dc:creator: Yao Wan

item.title: Generalized Fermat's principle and Snell's law for cone structures and applications
item.description: arXiv:2509.26492v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fermat's principle is fully generalized to the case where a smooth interface separates two cone structures -- Lorentz-Finsler lightcones -- representing wave propagation in a potentially inhomogeneous, anisotropic, time-dependent and discontinuous medium. The interface, wave source and receiver are assumed to be a hypersurface, a submanifold and a curve in the spacetime, respectively, of any causal character. For a trajectory to fulfill Fermat's principle -- i.e., to be a critical point of the arrival time functional -- its direction must change at the interface, obeying a precise condition that generalizes Snell's law of refraction when the wave crosses the interface, or the law of reflection when it remains in a single medium. Both laws are analyzed in detail to establish the conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of refracted and reflected trajectories, and to determine whether they actually minimize the arrival time. Applications to Zermelo's navigation problem and the determination of geodesics in discretized spacetimes are also emphasized.
item.dc:creator: Miguel \'Angel Javaloyes, Steen Markvorsen, Enrique Pend\'as-Recondo, Miguel S\'anchez

item.title: Gradient estimates and Liouville properties for the drifted Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2512.07389v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we discuss the validity of Liouville-type theorems involving the drifted Laplacian on complete, non-compact Riemannian manifolds endowed with a smooth vector field $X$. In particular, we prove new Liouville properties both for positive $X$-harmonic functions and for non-negative $X$-subharmonic functions which are in an $L^{p}$-space, $p\in(1,+\infty)$, with respect to any invariant measure for the operator. The main tool for the analysis is a local gradient estimate for positive solutions to the semilinear equation $\Delta_{X}u=F(u)$, which is valid if $F$ satisfies certain structural conditions and the Bakry-\'Emery-Ricci curvature associated to $X$ is bounded below. On the one hand, this estimate is used in a novel way to deduce the Liouville property for positive solutions and, on the other hand, it is used to construct cut-off functions for the $X$-Laplacian that yields the $L^{p}$-Liouville results.
item.dc:creator: Salvatore Lincastri

item.title: On a class of hypersurfaces of a product of two space forms
item.description: arXiv:2602.16087v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the notion of class $\mathcal{A}$, previously defined for hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{S}^n\times \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbb{S}^n$ and $\mathbb{H}^n$ denote the sphere and hyperbolic space, respectively, to hypersurfaces of a product $\mathbb{Q}_{c_1}^{k} \times \mathbb{Q}_{c_2}^{n-k+1}$, $2\leq k\leq n-1$, of two space forms with arbitrary constant curvatures $c_1$ and $c_2$. When $c_1$ and $c_2$ are not both equal to $0$, such a hypersurface is in class $\mathcal{A}$ if and only if it has a flat normal bundle when regarded as a submanifold of the underlying flat ambient space. We provide an explicit local construction of all hypersurfaces in class $\mathcal{A}$ that do not split in any open subset in terms of parallel families of hypersurfaces of the factors, and show how it simplifies for the hypersurfaces within this class that have a constant product angle function. We also show that hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature in class $\mathcal{A}$ are given in terms of parallel families of isoparametric hypersurfaces in each factor and a solution of a second order ODE. Finally, we classify hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature in class~$\mathcal{A}$ that have a constant product angle function.
item.dc:creator: Arnando Carvalho, Ruy Tojeiro

item.title: On Spherically Symmetric Sprays
item.description: arXiv:2604.11196v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies spherically symmetric sprays, i.e., sprays that are invariant under orthogonal transformations. We first establish a canonical form for such sprays, showing that their geodesic coefficients can be expressed as \(G^i = |y|\alpha(r,s) y^i + |y|^2\beta(r,s) x^i\), where \(r = |x|^2\) and \(s = \langle x,y\rangle/|y|\). For projectively flat spherically symmetric sprays -- which are directly related to Hilbert's fourth problem on characterizing metrics whose geodesics are straight lines -- we derive a complete classification of those with isotropic curvature, and in particular, we obtain the explicit form of those with zero curvature. Furthermore, we characterize sprays of weakly isotropic curvature in this class by a system of partial differential equations. These results may provide a unified framework for understanding symmetry and curvature in spray geometry and may offer new insights into the metrizability problem in Finsler geometry.
item.dc:creator: Yajing Gui, Benling Li

item.title: Hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{H}^2$ with constant sectional curvature
item.description: arXiv:2606.24686v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we classify the hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{H}^2$ with constant sectional curvature. In contrast to the case of $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^2$, the resulting examples for $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{H}^2$ exhibit greater diversity, and we construct a special example with non-constant product angle function. For $\mathbb{S}^2\times\mathbb{S}^2$, however, the product angle function of any constant sectional curvature hypersurface is identically zero. As a byproduct, we also classify the hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{H}^2$ with constant product angle function and constant mean curvature (or constant scalar curvature).
item.dc:creator: Haizhong Li, Luc Vrancken, Xianfeng Wang, Zeke Yao

item.title: Conformal boundary rigidity from null geodesic travel times
item.description: arXiv:2606.28689v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The gravitational field of a distant, isolated system is manifested by the conformally invariant Weyl tensor. Thus the conformal structure far from the system encodes the system's gravitational mass. It also encodes the causal structure, thereby linking it to the mass. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, this link led to a novel positive mass theorem of Page, Surya, and the second author \cite{PSW} which did not rely on any traditional energy condition. Here we ask whether that theorem has a rigidity case. Specifically, we consider all null geodesics in an asymptotically AdS spacetime that depart from the Penrose conformal infinity, travel through spacetime, and return to conformal infinity. If all such geodesics from a given point refocus at an antipodal point at infinity, is the spacetime conformal to anti-de Sitter space? It is easy to answer the question if the asymptotically AdS spacetime either (i) obeys the null energy condition in 3 or 4 spacetime dimensions, or (ii) is static (in any dimension), and we give simple proofs in those cases. We then answer the question in the case of globally stationary, asymptotically AdS spacetimes, by applying the theory of magnetic geodesics on the Riemannian manifold-with-boundary obtained by quotienting by the stationary Killing vector field. The question has an analogue for asymptotically flat spacetimes, which we also discuss.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Paternain, Eric Woolgar

item.title: Finite-Time Singularities of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow with Quantitatively Precise Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.03152v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For each integer $K\geq2$ when $n\geq4$, and for $K=2,3,4$ when $n=3$, we construct an almost-calibrated Lagrangian mean curvature flow $L_K(t)$ in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, starting from initial data arbitrarily close to being special Lagrangian, which develops a finite-time Type II singularity at time $T$ with the explicit curvature blow up rate \[ \sup_{L_{K}(t)} |\mathbf{A}_{L_{K}(t)}| \sim (T-t)^{-K/2} \qquad \text{as } t\nearrow T . \] The tangent flow at the singularity is a transverse pair of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian cones, while the Type II blow-up limit is a smooth cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularization. This gives a quantitative construction of Type II blow-up for a fully nonlinear parabolic PDE arising from cohomogeneity-one Lagrangian mean curvature flow. Our construction is based on a modulation analysis around a shrinking family of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularizations, using the perturbative spectral theory developed in the companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Maxwell Stolarski, Wei-Bo Su

item.title: Invariant forms compute the Dolbeault cohomology of complex nilmanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.26786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the inclusion of left-invariant forms into the Dolbeault complex of a compact nilmanifold $M$ endowed with a left-invariant complex structure $J$ induces an isomorphism in cohomology in every bidegree, settling a long-standing conjecture originating from a question of Console-Fino and Cordero-Fern\'andez-Gray-Ugarte. As consequences, we show that small deformations of $J$ are still invariant, as conjectured by Hasegawa, and that Bott-Chern, Aeppli, and Fr\"olicher invariants are computed by invariant forms and are independent of the lattice, settling a conjecture of Angella on Bott-Chern cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Keizo Hasegawa, Lorenzo Sillari, Adriano Tomassini

item.title: The sharp volume gap for K\"ahler manifolds with positive Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2608.08193v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a sharp volume gap estimate: if an $n$-dimensional compact K\"ahler manifold $(X, \omega)$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(\omega)\ge (n+1)\omega$ and $X\not\cong \mathbb{P}^n$, then $\mathrm{vol}(X, \omega)\le \frac{2n^n}{(n+1)^n}\mathrm{vol}(\mathbb{P}^n,\omega_{\mathrm{FS}})=\frac{2^{n+1} \, \pi^n \, n^n}{(n+1)^n}$. Moreover $\mathrm{vol}(X, \omega)= \frac{2^{n+1} \, \pi^n \, n^n}{(n+1)^n}$ occurs if and only if $(X, \omega)$ is biholomorphically isometric to the K\"ahler-Einstein metric on the quadric hypersurface $Q^n$ or on the product $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We also obtain sharp volume gap estimates for K-semistable toric log Fano pairs.
item.dc:creator: Chi Li, Minghao Miao, Kewei Zhang

item.title: The stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb{R}^{7}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.15720v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a Green-function proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb R^7$ for smooth, connected, complete, two-sided stable minimal hypersurfaces, thus resolving the last case of the stable Bernstein problem.
item.dc:creator: Han Hong, Haizhong Li, Gaoming Wang

item.title: Infinitesimmaly homogeneous manifolds with symplectic and almost contact structure groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.19568v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study infinitesimally homogeneous affine manifolds with prescribed structure groups. First, for the real symplectic group $\operatorname{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)$, we prove that the corresponding infinitesimally homogeneous structures are precisely flat torsion-free symplectic affine structures. Second, for \(\operatorname{U}(n)\times\{1\}\), whose \(G\)-structures are equivalent to almost contact metric data, we classify the torsion-free characteristic tensors and obtain the general torsional case by invariant deformation. The admissible torsion and inner-torsion parameters are governed by a single algebraic relation, and the horizontal distribution is contact precisely when a certain combination of these parameters does not vanish. We also describe the compatible connections and relate the torsion-free branches to trans-Sasakian geometry.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Alberto Mar\'in Arango, Alejandro Pinilla Barrera

item.title: Conformal Killing--Yano Ricci solitons: Basic structure and first examples
item.description: arXiv:2609.23424v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a conformal Killing-Yano Ricci soliton, coupling conformal Ricci soliton geometry to conformal Killing-Yano 2-forms via the divergence of the form. In four-dimensional Lorentzian signature, the principal conformal structure is not preserved under non-trivial conformal deformation, so the associated form on local Kerr-NUT-(A)dS backgrounds is not closed. For Einstein backgrounds in any dimension and signature, integrability forces the form to be Killing for the background and conformal Killing for the necessarily Einstein soliton metric, with the conformal factor satisfying eigenvalue and Obata-type Hessian equations; the coupling fixes the Einstein constant. Vanishing coupling reduces the data to Killing data on the fiber; otherwise the soliton metric is Ricci-flat. Locally the background is a warped product. In the compact Riemannian case, the manifold is the round sphere. Explicit static spherically symmetric and BTZ constructions are given, with applications to exact geometries in general relativity.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadjavad Habibivostakolaei, Abbas M. Sherif, Yen-Kheng Lim

item.title: Timelike surfaces of constant mean and constant Gaussian curvature in anti-de Sitter 3-space via loop groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.33504v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The loop group description of surfaces whose Gauss map is Lorentz harmonic is known for timelike surfaces of constant mean curvature in the flat Lorentzian 3-space, and for surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in the 3-sphere. We carry out the corresponding construction for timelike surfaces in anti-de Sitter 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3_1\cong SL(2,\mathbb{R})$: those of constant mean curvature, whose Gauss map is harmonic for the conformal structure of the first fundamental form, and those of constant Gaussian curvature $K>-1$, $K\neq0$, whose Gauss map is then an immersion and is harmonic for the second fundamental form. For both classes we prove the harmonicity characterization, recover the surfaces from extended frames by Sym-Bobenko-type formulas, and solve the geometric Cauchy problem by the generalized DPW method, with potentials written explicitly in terms of the data and no normalization of the Gauss map. We then show that the two constructions differ only by a normalization: after the substitution $\lambda=\zeta^2$ and a constant gauge, a constant mean curvature extended frame $\hat F$ is an extended frame of its Gauss map, and the maps $\hat F|_{\lambda=e^{4\theta}}\exp(\theta e_3)\hat F|_{\lambda=1}^{-1}$ and $e_3\hat F|_{\lambda=e^{4\theta}}e_3\exp(\theta e_3)\hat F|_{\lambda=1}^{-1}$, with $e_3=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1)$, are timelike surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature $1/\sinh^2\theta$ and $-1/\cosh^2\theta$ wherever the constant mean curvature surface is not flat. The first is the classical parallel surface, the second its polar surface. Explicit families, with extended frames and surfaces in closed form, illustrate the constructions.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Bravo-Gadea

item.title: Codimension Reduction of Minimal Submanifolds with Flat Normal Bundle in Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.07789v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $x:M^n\to\mathbb{S}^{n+q}$ be a minimal immersion of a complete connected manifold with flat normal bundle, where $n\ge3$ and $q\ge2$. We prove that if the squared norm $S$ of the second fundamental form satisfies $S\le 2n$, then either $x(M)$ is contained in a fixed totally geodesic subsphere $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, or $x:M\to x(M)$ is a Riemannian covering onto a standard minimal product of three spheres with $S\equiv 2n$. We also prove that $x(M)$ is contained in a fixed totally geodesic subsphere $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$ under the assumption $S+\lambda_2\le 2n+\frac{2n}{3n-2}$, where $\lambda_2$ is the second largest eigenvalue of the Gram matrix of the shape operators.
item.dc:creator: Juan Li, Zhiyuan Xu

item.title: Almost-splitting of spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10051v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an almost-splitting theorem for spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds in the spirit of the celebrated Riemannian result due to Cheeger and Colding. More concretely, we show that if a globally hyperbolic spacetime with timelike sectional curvature bounded below by a nonpositive constant close to zero contains a long maximizing timelike segment, then causal diamonds along that segment are close in the Lorentzian Gromov--Hausdorff sense of Minguzzi--Suhr to those in a product metric spacetime. Our result can be interpreted as a quantitative analogue of the Lorentzian splitting theorem for spacetimes with nonnegative timelike sectional curvature by Beem--Ehrlich--Markvorsen--Galloway. In contrast to the Riemannian setting, the timelike sectional curvature bound cannot be replaced by Ricci-flatness, as the small mass limit of the Schwarzschild exterior geometry shows.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Gigli, Melanie Graf, Robert J. McCann, Argam Ohanyan, Eric Woolgar, Matteo Zanardini

item.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.18599v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.
item.dc:creator: Antonio De Rosa, Aria Halavati

item.title: Scalar curvature integrals on geodesic balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.29596v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove bounds for scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds with nonnegative sectional curvature. In every dimension $n\ge3$, when the asymptotic volume ratio is close to one, we obtain upper and lower estimates with the sharp first-order coefficient and a quadratic remainder. The leading terms involve the asymptotic and local volume deficits, respectively. Rotationally symmetric examples show that both first-order coefficients are optimal and that a quadratic remainder is necessary in the upper bound. For dimensions three, four, and five we give estimates for any positive asymptotic volume ratio. When the center is a pole, we give an estimate in dimension three under nonnegative Ricci curvature and in every dimension $n\ge4$ under nonnegative sectional curvature. This estimate is sharp when the asymptotic volume ratio is at most $2^{-(n-1)}$.
item.dc:creator: Qixuan Hu

item.title: The cross quadratic bisectional curvature of K\"{a}hler $C$-spaces of classical type
item.description: arXiv:2610.39012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we show that any K\"{a}hler $C$-space of classical type has nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature. As a consequence, such manifolds are Fano. This confirms a substantial part of a conjecture of Ni-Zheng (Conjecture 1.5 in \cite{NZ}).
item.dc:creator: Run-Qiang Jian, Zhuhong Zhang

item.title: Spectral gaps near one quarter for Weil--Petersson random surfaces with growing cusp number
item.description: arXiv:2611.01477v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ with $n=n(g)\ge1$ labelled cusps converges in probability to $1/4$ as $g\to\infty$, for every sequence $n=o(\sqrt g)$.
